content.title: Rizq: A Story of Unseen Abundance
content.subtitle: We lament what we lack; did we count what we have?
content.body:
What do we really mean by rizq? A substantial salary? A big house? An expensive car? A comfortable life? But is rizq really that?

One day, you may have plenty of money. But the person who asks, “Baba, have you eaten?” may no longer be there. You may have a big house, but one of the familiar faces waiting to open the door may be gone. Many things may be added to your life, while some people whose presence feels ordinary today may then be only memories. Perhaps then we will understand that rizq was not only material wealth and luxury.

Some Rizq Comes as People

After marriage, many people say, “My rizq has increased.” We immediately start calculating: How much did the salary increase? How much profit came from the business? What new possessions arrived? As if rizq could be measured in numbers or money.

But very few notice that perhaps Allah has sent someone into our lives with whom talking washes away the day’s exhaustion. Someone beside whom even a cup of tea brings peace. Someone before whom we do not have to hide our failures. Someone whose silence feels like a refuge. Tell me, isn’t such a person rizq?

Count Your Rizq Again Today

When was the last time you looked at your mother and thought, “She still makes dua for me”? When was the last time you considered your father’s presence a blessing? When was the last time you looked at your spouse and thought, “Why did Allah make this person part of my life?” When was the last time you returned home and thought, “Alhamdulillah, I have a home to return to”?

Perhaps before counting rizq through our bank balance, we should look at our lives. Some of Allah’s priceless blessings cannot be measured in numbers. Some rizq comes as people, some as relationships, and some as peace. Some rizq surrounds us so quietly that we do not realize how rich we were until we lose it.

So today, let us not count only what we do not have. Let us look at what we still have. Perhaps then we will say, “Alhamdulillah! Without even asking, my Lord has filled my life with countless, immeasurable rizq.”
